name: La Mamounia
insider_take: This legendary palace hotel has been the crown jewel of Marrakech since 1923, where Winston Churchill painted and movie stars escaped to Morocco's most enchanting oasis.
whats_special: La Mamounia sits on royal gardens gifted by Sultan Sidi Mohammed Ben Abdullah in the 18th century, featuring the same olive and orange groves that have flourished for over 200 years. The hotel's Art Deco design seamlessly blends with traditional Moroccan architecture, creating spaces so stunning that Churchill called it "the most lovely spot in the whole world."
pro_tip: Book the Churchill Bar for sunset cocktails – it's where the former Prime Minister spent countless evenings, and the terrace offers unobstructed views of the Atlas Mountains just as he painted them.
dont_miss: The hotel's legendary hammam spa experience in a 2,500-square-meter sanctuary, and a stroll through the historic Majorelle Garden just 10 minutes away – once owned by Yves Saint Laurent and featuring the world's most photographed cobalt blue villa.
pros: Legendary palace hotel with rich Moroccan heritage and royal history
Spectacular 17-acre gardens with century-old olive trees and exotic plants
World-class spa offering traditional hammam and luxury wellness treatments
Multiple acclaimed restaurants featuring Moroccan and international cuisine
Prime location near Marrakech's historic medina and souks
cons: Formal atmosphere may not suit casual travelers
